checks.message: New S3 bucket - verify Block Public Access is enabled
checks.context: Public S3 buckets are the #1 cause of AWS data breaches. Billions of records have been exposed this way. Run `aws s3api put-public-access-block` immediately after creation.

checks.message: Object Lock not enabled, so bucket objects can be overwritten or deleted immediately
checks.context: Object Lock provides WORM (write-once-read-many) protection. Without it, ransomware or a compromised credential can delete or overwrite all objects instantly. Required by many compliance frameworks (SEC 17a-4, HIPAA, CJIS). Warning: Object Lock cannot be disabled once enabled and requires versioning.

checks.message: BlockPublicAcls not set to true in public access block configuration
checks.context: Without BlockPublicAcls=true, new public ACLs can still be applied to objects in this bucket, making them publicly readable.

checks.message: IgnorePublicAcls not set to true in public access block configuration
checks.context: Without IgnorePublicAcls=true, existing public ACLs on objects still grant public access even if new ones are blocked.

checks.message: BlockPublicPolicy not set to true in public access block configuration
checks.context: Without BlockPublicPolicy=true, bucket policies that grant public access can still be applied.

checks.message: RestrictPublicBuckets not set to true in public access block configuration
checks.context: Without RestrictPublicBuckets=true, existing public bucket policies still grant public and cross-account access.

checks.message: Bucket ACL set to public-read
checks.context: This makes every object in the bucket readable by anyone on the internet - no credentials required. If you need to share files publicly, use a CloudFront distribution with an Origin Access Identity instead.

checks.message: Bucket ACL set to public-read-write
checks.context: Anyone on the internet can read AND write to this bucket. This is almost never intentional and can lead to data injection, ransomware uploads, or massive egress charges from abuse.

checks.message: Prefer SSE-KMS over SSE-S3 for stronger key control
checks.context: SSE-S3 uses a key managed entirely by AWS with no audit trail. SSE-KMS gives you key rotation, CloudTrail logs of every decryption, and the ability to revoke access instantly by disabling the key.

checks.message: MFA Delete not enabled. Consider enabling for critical buckets
checks.context: Versioning alone doesn't prevent deletion; it just keeps old versions. MFA Delete requires a second factor to permanently delete versions, protecting against both accidental deletion and ransomware.

checks.message: Review bucket policy for wildcard principals or actions
checks.context: Bucket policies with Principal:* or Action:s3:* can expose your bucket to the entire internet or grant excessive permissions. Always scope to specific principals, actions, and resources.

checks.message: Bucket deletion is permanent and irreversible
checks.context: Deleting an S3 bucket removes all objects and cannot be undone. Bucket names are globally unique - once deleted, another AWS account could claim the same name, potentially breaking application references.

checks.message: Bulk object deletion - verify bucket has versioning enabled
checks.context: Without versioning, deleted objects are permanently gone. This operation can delete thousands of objects in a single call. Run with a dry-run or list the objects first to confirm the scope.

checks.message: File uploaded with public-read ACL
checks.context: This object will be accessible to anyone with the URL - no AWS credentials needed. A common mistake when testing that gets forgotten and left public. Use a pre-signed URL for temporary sharing instead.

checks.message: SSL verification disabled
checks.context: Disabling SSL verification exposes your data and credentials to man-in-the-middle attacks. If you're hitting a proxy or cert error, fix the certificate trust chain - don't bypass it.

checks.message: Server-side encryption not explicitly specified for upload
checks.context: While S3 default encryption may be configured at the bucket level, explicitly specifying a customer-managed KMS key ensures the object is encrypted under your key policy, with full control over rotation, access, and audit. Without --sse-kms-key-id, S3 falls back to the AWS-managed key (aws/s3) which you cannot control or rotate on your own schedule.

checks.message: Syncing with public-read ACL - all synced objects will be publicly accessible
checks.context: Every file in this sync operation will be readable by anyone on the internet. A single sync of the wrong directory can expose source code, credentials, or customer data.

checks.message: --delete flag will permanently remove files not present in the source
checks.context: This is a common cause of accidental data loss. Files deleted from S3 without versioning enabled are unrecoverable. Run with --dryrun first to preview what will be deleted.

checks.message: Recursive delete will remove ALL objects under the prefix
checks.context: This can wipe an entire bucket in seconds. Without versioning enabled, every deleted object is gone permanently. Always run with --dryrun first to preview what will be removed.

checks.message: S3 delete operation - this may be irreversible
checks.context: If the bucket does not have versioning enabled, deleted objects are gone permanently. There is no recycle bin. Run `aws s3 ls` first to confirm the target.

checks.message: Object uploaded with public-read ACL
checks.context: This object is readable by anyone on the internet without authentication. Use pre-signed URLs for temporary access instead of making objects permanently public.

checks.message: Ensure you are not downloading sensitive data to an insecure location
checks.context: Downloading secrets, credentials, or PII to a local machine or shared filesystem can inadvertently expose sensitive data. Verify the destination path is appropriate.

checks.message: Removing Block Public Access - bucket may become publicly accessible
checks.context: Deleting the public access block removes all four protections (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets). Any existing public ACLs or bucket policies will immediately take effect, potentially exposing data to the internet.

checks.message: Removing explicit bucket encryption configuration
checks.context: Since January 2023, S3 automatically encrypts all new objects with SSE-S3 even without a bucket-level configuration. However, removing an SSE-KMS configuration means new objects will no longer be encrypted with your KMS key, losing CloudTrail decrypt audit trail and the ability to revoke access by disabling the key.

checks.message: Object deletion is permanent unless versioning is enabled on the bucket
checks.context: Without versioning, deleted objects are gone forever. With versioning, a delete marker is placed but the object can be recovered. Verify the bucket's versioning status before deleting.
